comments.value:
This especially useful for something like the DiverX ContactGlove which uses 107 or 177 bits to give finger tracking.

Other possible additions:

- lower resolution ints and floats would be another possibility as well. I don't need to use 8 bits just to switch between a few outfits.

- changing from a maximum number of bits to a maximum number of bits/second updates combined with the priority would be nice as well since various parameters are not updated very frequently at all.

Face tracking is starting to become standard, and consumes a huge chunk of params. Avatar state is another one which people are consuming it for synced purposes.

Ideally there would be native face tracking and state systems which would preclude the need to run OSC or stash things in params to get around this; but realistically it's not going to happen. 

So in liu of you implementing native solutions which wouldn't consume parameter space, please:

**  Update the param space to a word instead of a byte. **

 Double bonus points if you put in a short-short 4-bit integer option.

This would push from 256 bits to 65.5k which would at least give a lot more headroom.

The issue here is, the community has already worked around this with animation layers and local parameter stuff. So now you have drastically more complex animation layers just to get around you limiting the parameter size. You've traded one byte of network for basically every avatar running multiple frame sweeps to pack and unpack synced params.

The community will get around this, you're just making it less efficent. Please just do the right thing and either provide native resources to remove the things consuming large amount of parameter space _OR_ update param space to something that isn't a constant burden and (ideally) increase OSC response time.

Yup, face tracking takes a lot of parameters, either getting double the size, or having those FT parameters synced by VRChat without being counted in the avatar memory space would be a huge improvement !

details:
I know we already went from 128 to 256, but with the addition of OSC and people taking full advantage of it, even 256 bits is limiting for many advanced users. Especially with the fact that ALL parameters that need to be controlled by the expression menu have to be networked.
I don't understand why there's even a limit this low when you consider players voices and IK movement must be so, so much more data in transmission. Or am I mistaken?
Please consider upping the amount of parameters we are allowed to use on avatars please. There have been many cases where I've had to straight up ditch an idea on my avatar despite it being within my medium/poor constraints because I don't have enough parameter space. Full face and eye tracking alone can easily use up to 150 bits. Want haptics too? Maybe a heart rate display? Not all happening at the same time without sacrifice.
I have a HUD on my avatar that uses 32 bits for adjusting the opacity/size/depth and it doesn't even need to be networked, it's local only... There's just so many issues that seem heavily overlooked.
I think a perfect system would be something along the lines of this:
- More networked parameters, I think 512 would be way more than enough. It should be a limit nobody would need to hit, so nobody can complain. But still low enough to where it has no impact on players experiences. Could be limited to PC only too since most OSC features that could exceed 256 bits only work on PC anyway.
Because platform parameter sync is based on both the parameter names and order, it would be easy for creators to keep PC/Quest avatar sync despite a difference in parameter count across both platforms. 
- Parameter priority support, higher priority = faster sync
- Possibly limit avatars based on network load rather than the amount of parameters they use. Rate of the lowest priority parameters can be auto limited. I don't see why someone can't have 10+ sliders just for avatar lighting when they become static values once used anyway.
They aren't updating in real time and dont need to sync fast when updated either. You could even create a new float type, realtime Vs static. Static only updates when the wheel is closed, then pushes values to the server at low intervals whereas realtime floats use IK sync. Again, for something like a brightness slider, a very low rate is needed just so late joiners can see the updated value.
- Allow local parameters to be controlled by the expression menu
- Slightly unrelated but, local only contacts that don't affect performance stats for OSC haptics, local only menu's on avatars and so on. Would be a perfect solution for people who use haptics in VR and have to constrain themselves in club worlds that have performance rank limits. It's very annoying that an avatar is deemed 'worse performance' for a feature most people set up to be local only with the isLocal parameter anyway. Just, why?
Hope this can be looked into further, thank you!
title: Can we get even more parameters please?
